outcome: No result found that resolves, partially resolves, or moves a bound on whether every reversible cellular automaton in three or more dimensions is locally reversible; the problem remains stated as open in the most recent secondary source found (the current English Wikipedia article on reversible cellular automata).
summary: The problem asks whether every reversible cellular automaton (CA) in three or more spatial dimensions is 'locally reversible' — i.e., realizable as a composition of local, reversible logic-gate-like steps (in the sense made precise by Kari 1996 and Durand-Lose 2001), analogous to what is known for one and two dimensions. I read the current (2026) English Wikipedia article on reversible cellular automata, which still lists this as an open problem under 'Billiard-ball computation and low-power computing': 'Kari (1996) showed that for one- and two-dimensional automata the answer is positive, and Durand-Lose (2001) showed that any reversible cellular automaton could be simulated by a (possibly different) locally reversible cellular automaton. However, the question of whether every reversible transition function is locally reversible remains open for dimensions higher than two.' No citation to any 2024-2026 work appears there. I then searched arXiv and the general web for any paper addressing local reversibility of 3D+ reversible CAs specifically, and found only tangential or unrelated work: (1) Durand-Lose's much older (pre-2024) theorem that any d-dimensional reversible CA can be written as a composition of d+1 block permutations (a block-cellular-automaton representation theorem, proving a 1990 Toffoli–Margolus conjecture) — this is a different notion (global block-decomposition, not local-gate reversibility) and predates the window regardless; (2) 'New classes of reversible cellular automata' (arXiv 2411.00721, Nov 2024, published in Designs, Codes and Cryptography 2026) — this concerns 'proper liftings' of Boolean functions parameterized by bit-width k, an unrelated notion of 'dimension'; (3) 'A Reversibility Characterization of Locally Finite Groups by Cellular Automata' (arXiv 2606.29958, 2026) — concerns CA over group shifts and locally finite groups, not the 3D local-reversibility question; (4) a 2025 AUTOMATA proceedings paper on number-conserving CA in three dimensions, which is a different conjecture (only trivial number-conserving reversible CAs exist) about a different notion of 'three-dimensional' constraint; (5) AutomataGPT (2026), an LLM-based system for forecasting and inferring CA update rules from data — this is unrelated AI-for-CA work but does not touch reversibility structure theorems, let alone this specific open problem. No preprint, announcement, or digested result of any kind addresses this problem in the 26 January 2024 - present window, and no AI system is credited with, or connected to, any progress on it.
competing_reading: None of the tangentially related papers found (block-CA representation, Boolean-function liftings, locally-finite-group CA, number-conserving CA, AutomataGPT) could plausibly be read as bearing on this exact scope question even under a generous reading; they concern different structures or different notions of 'dimension'/'reversibility'. There is no genuine ambiguity here to flag.
what_would_settle_it: A paper proving or disproving that every reversible CA in 3+ dimensions decomposes into locally reversible (reversible-logic-gate) steps, or a paper narrowing the question (e.g., resolving it for a restricted class of 3D CAs), which would at minimum warrant a 'partial' classification. Absent that, continued citation of the problem as open in a current survey or the Wikipedia article itself is the best available confirmation of the status quo.
